blocks.md: This lesson covers the book's section on **Dual Failure Modes of Policy Training**. Read the excerpt, then test yourself below.

blocks.source: Vol IV, Policy Training, § Dual Failure Modes of Policy Training
blocks.md: A robot arm executing a learned trajectory can track every waypoint cleanly across hundreds of simulation episodes and still arrive at its first physical deployment with no evidence about whether it will fracture a latch. In classical robotics, control design begins with an explicit analytical model of the plant: engineers write down kinematic equations, inertia matrices, stability margins, and torque limits where they can be systematically inspected and verified.

blocks.md: Compare your answer with the book's claim: A simulator's contact model decides what the optimizer learns, and a soft penalty spring lets a policy pass through contacts the real plate would resist.

questions.q: The section **Dual Failure Modes of Policy Training** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: Posing the task as an MDP makes the engineer-written reward and discount the whole objective, so the optimizer exploits any omitted or mismeasured term.
A simulator's contact model decides what the optimizer learns, and a soft penalty spring lets a policy pass through contacts the real plate would resist.
Chunked imitation fits a horizon of actions with a Huber penalty on normalized residuals, which buys outlier robustness, not smoothness or feasibility.

A decoder chosen for multimodality must fit the proposal deadline, since latency is encoding plus every dependent decoder evaluation, so the head and evaluation count that training picks decide schedulability.
